definitions.gloss: precariousness; the quality of being on the edge of failure
definitions.explanation: The nominalized form of {危|あや}うい. It names a fragile, unstable quality that could tip into disaster at any moment — often used admiringly of art, performance, or beauty as well as critically of situations.

examples.japanese: その{計画|けいかく}の{危|あや}うさに{気|き}づいた。
examples.english: I noticed how precarious that plan was.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{歌|うた}には{危|あや}うさと{美|うつく}しさがある。
examples.english: Her singing has both a fragility and a beauty to it.

examples.japanese: {好調|こうちょう}に{見|み}えるこの{経済|けいざい}にも、{一部|いちぶ}の{専門家|せんもんか}は{危|あや}うさを{感|かん}じている。
examples.english: Even in this economy, which looks strong, some experts sense a fragility.

notes:
Formed from the i-adjective {危|あや}うい plus the nominalizing suffix 〜さ. Written language more than conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {危|あや}うさを{感|かん}じる: to sense a precariousness
- {危|あや}うさをはらむ: to contain an element of danger
- {危|あや}うさが{漂|ただよ}う: an air of fragility hangs over something
- ぎりぎりの{危|あや}うさ: a razor's-edge precariousness

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {危|あぶ}なさ: dangerousness — plainer and more physical; {危|あや}うさ is more literary and often admiring
- {危険|きけん}{性|せい}: riskiness — neutral and analytical, used in reports and assessments
